explanation: Insert words into a character trie. Search follows literal edges; a dot recursively tries every child at that position. Accept only when the entire pattern ends at a terminal node.
timeComplexity: O(L) expected insertion; O(T) worst-case search over T stored trie nodes. Insertion follows L edges; a wildcard search may visit every stored trie node up to the pattern depth.
spaceComplexity: O(T) stored nodes; O(L) search recursion for pattern length L. Stored prefixes occupy T nodes and recursive search has at most L+1 frames.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C# implementation, reusing and refining the repository-authored Blind75 algorithm fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: At each pattern position, a literal follows its one matching trie edge and a dot considers every existing child edge. This enumerates exactly all stored paths whose characters agree with the pattern. Accepting only a terminal node after the entire pattern is consumed ensures equal word length and complete-word matching.
walkthrough: Add "map" and "mat". Pattern "ma." matches either final letter, and "m.." also matches a three-letter stored word. Pattern "maps" is too long and fails. Return query results [true,true,false]. The arrays describe calls on one instance in order; expected contains only Search booleans, omitting AddWord returns.
edgeCases: A dot matches exactly one character, never an arbitrary string.
Literal searches require a complete stored word.
Adding an already stored word does not change search results.
